steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8x8-inch square pan; line with greased foil.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Rub in butter using your hands or a pastry blender to form a crumbly mixture.
Press 2 cups oat mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan.
Spread jam to within 1/4 inch of the edge.
Sprinkle remaining crumb mixture on top; press down lightly into jam.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 35 to 40 minutes.
Allow to cool before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Raspberry Oatmeal Cookie Bars
raw_recipe.description: This oatmeal cookie bar recipe is easy to make with seedless raspberry jam sandwiched between buttery brown sugar-oat cookie crusts for a sweet treat.

video.description: When the cookie cravings come on strong, there’s no need to worry, because these mix up fast and bake up incredibly delicious. Combine brown sugar with flour, baking soda, salt and rolled oats. Work in butter until you form a crumbly mixture, most of which you’ll press into a baking pan. Spread a whole bunch of yummy raspberry jam over it, then top with more crust crumbles. Bake until browned, then go pour yourself a glass of milk while they cool—soon you’ll get the cookie satisfaction you deserve!

review.reviewBody: I make these all the time. I've made some modifications to make them healthier (sub applesauce for some of butter, whole wheat pastry flour, less sugar, less jam filling), and my kids love them. If you make a double batch and substitute an egg for 1/4 cup of the butter, they don't crumble as much. I melt the butter and just stir it in.

I really like these. I did bump them up a bit this time though. I used seedless blackberry Polaner All Fruit and slightly less than called for (a double batch would call for 12oz and I used a 10oz jar). I made a double batch in a 9x13" pan and greased it really well and had no trouble getting it out. I also sprinkled the jam with a few handfuls of white and semi-sweet chocolate chips before adding the final topping layer and pressing it all in. The key to this not crumbling is to really work the SOFTENED butter into the dry ingredients with your hand. If you just stir it, it won't work enough of the fat through it and it will fall apart after it's baked. All in all, a nice, sweet, easy, cookie.

Really easy and lends itself to modifications for personal preferences. I buttered the baking dish but didn't foil, and the bars came out just fine. I added about 1/4 c chopped pecans that I'd roasted in advance, added 1/2 tsp vanilla extract to the oatmeal mix after incorporating butter, and reduced the sugar to about 1/3 cup. To the jam I added 1/2 tsp lemon juice and warmed the jam slightly in the microwave before spreading. I baked the bottom crust for about 10 minutes before adding the jam. Thanks for a great recipe!

This recipe is a fantastic starting point! I have used it perhaps eight times now, and continue to make small changes that improve it. I double the ingredients and bake in a 9"x13" pan. Properly prepping the pan will allow you to lift the entire baked slab out later, after cooling. Butter the pan, then add a half-sheet of parchment paper (12"x16"), pressing it into place, up the sides of the pan, into the corners, etc. Then butter the parchment paper, too. Assemble the oat mixture and press most of it (3/4 or so, you can eyeball it) into the lined pan, to make the bottom 'crust'. Spread your chosen jam evenly over the crust, covering it all the way to the edge. You will likely need more jam than the recipe calls for. Scatter the remaining oat mixture over the top, and bake. So easy! When your pan has completely cooled, you can pull up on the parchment paper and transfer the slab to a cutting board. Use a sharp chef knife. Chill the slab if it does not cut cleanly. Cut about 1/2" off each edge of the slab: the very-brown and crispy part. I don't want those hard edges on my bars, but they are great for nibbling on separately. Then cut the remainder of the slab into bars. Experiment with your own additions! Add spices like cinnamon or clove, or chopped nuts, to the dry ingredients. Add vanilla or almond extract to the softened butter, before adding the butter to the dry ingredients. Add dark chocolate chips on top of your jam layer, before topping with the remaining oat mixture. Such a fun and versatile recipe! Everyone raves about these bars! The attached photo shows today's masterpiece: red currant jelly, dark chocolate chips, slivered almonds, almond and vanilla extracts, and cinnamon and clove

This recipe is great. I used 2 punnets (125g each) of fresh raspberries and mashed them in with remaining crumb mixture for the topping. Excellent. I cut them smallish and freeze them for a quick after dinner dessert or with a cup of tea for a morning snack.

I enjoy this recipe very much! The bars are delicious; they taste and look like they are professionally made in a bakery! I made some changes because I wanted to use up some ingredients that I had at home. Because I wanted to use up my quinoa flakes that are expiring, I decided to used 1/2 cup quinoa flakes and 1/2 cup rolled oats instead of the full cup of oats that the recipe calls for. Instead of raspberry jam, I used my freshly made homemade strawberry mango jam. Like another reviewer, I also processed all of the crumb ingredients in my food processor (butter cut in small cubes) and lined my 8×8 baking sheet with parchment paper. That is it -- easy-peasy!

This recipe is super easy. It does, however, need more flavoring. The first time I made these they were so bland. The next time I added a teaspoon of cinnamon and a teaspoon of vanilla. That made a huge difference. I also put most of the cookie mix on the bottom, used 10 oz. of jam, and put the rest of the cookie mix on top. Make sure not to over bake.

Really needs an egg added; super crumbly. I added cinnamon to dry ingredients, and 1/4 tsp almond oil and tsp vanilla to jam. Next time, definitely adding egg. Pre-baked bottom as others suggested; next time 20 minutes for bottom. It’s tasty as something to crumble with vanilla bean ice cream, it’s just messy tasty.

I have made it several times and only changed two things. The first is to double the recipe, and use a larger pan, of course. The second was that it seemed to me that the rasperry jam itself, especially the seedless stuff, was a bit bland, and lacking in flavor. I solved this by sprinkling about a cup and a half of chopped up frozen raspberries onto the top of the jam, before adding the final layer of topping and baking it. Adds a bit of raspberry punchiness to the recipe.

Delicious is right! we really enjoyed these.

I used Bob's Red Mill quick cooking steel cuts oats since that is what I had. otherwise, made it as written. 

 I made my own jam using 2 cups of frozen raspberries and 1 cup sugar. boil and stir constantly for 8 minutes. Added some lemon juice (@2 tsp?).

Not sure what else to say. These were easy and yummy! will make again!

So easy and so good. I have a lot of homemade jam and am always looking for ways to serve it . Will make again.

So I made this with peach jam that I made last year - I made the largest size I also used 2 cups instead of the 1 1/2 and I had coffee cake crumbs in the fridge that I never made a coffee cake for - it's currently baking. Thanks for the recipe!

My entire family loved these. Few changes I made: added 1/2 tsp vanilla to the raspberry jam; substituted 3 tablespoons coconut oil for butter as I did not have enough left. Planning to make a double batch next!

I didn't feel like looking for the right size pan, so I used a 9"x15" one and made 1 1/2 times the recipe. I only had 1/2 cup of brown sugar so I put in a couple of tablespoons of Splenda/sugar mixture. I made these to use up some blueberry sauce I had made. Mixed in some raspberry jam for better consistency. They turned out great, holding together with not too many crumbs. Already eaten more than I should have.
Delicious! I did make about 50% more of the cookie portion to allow a thicker cookie crust on top! This was a hit!
I’ve made these numerous times over the past 8 or so years. We love Raspberry, but I’ve also made them using Blueberry Jam and they are equally good!

I have made these bars in the past and they are delicious! I tried doubling the recipe for a party, but the directions are not doubled. Where it says 2 cups of crumbs should be put in the bottom of the pan, it should read 4 cups for a doubled recipe in a 13 x 9 pan. As it turns out the raspberry preserves sunk with very little bottom crust. Next time I'll know better.

A new family favorite! I used the recipe for a double batch, adding 1 tsp of cinnamon and replacing the raspberry jam with marionberry fruit spread. I used a 13 x 9 pan with parchment paper instead of foil.

Nostalgic for me! Love it! I doubled the recipe to use a 13x9 pan and it was perfect. I also added a quarter can of blueberries, drained, to the filling like my mom used to . I made it for my sister on her birthday. She was so happy!
